toulousecapitole.name: Capitole
toulousecapitole.slogan: A 135-metre pink-brick facade that is the face of the Ville Rose.
toulousecapitole.line: Its eight Corinthian columns recall the eight capitouls, the city magistrates who once governed Toulouse from this site.

toulousesaintsernin.name: Basilica of Saint-Sernin
toulousesaintsernin.slogan: Pilgrims' brick bell tower, rising over the road to Compostela.
toulousesaintsernin.line: Pope Urban II consecrated its altar on 24 May 1096, and it now stands on the UNESCO list of Santiago de Compostela routes.

albicathedral.name: Albi Cathedral
albicathedral.slogan: A brick fortress of God, rose-red above the Tarn.
albicathedral.line: Built between 1282 and 1480, it is claimed to be the largest brick building in the world.

toulousejacobins.name: Couvent des Jacobins
toulousejacobins.slogan: One slender column that blooms into a stone palm tree.
toulousejacobins.line: The choir vault springs from a single column and spreads into 22 ribs like palm leaves.

cordesgrandrue.name: Cordes-sur-Ciel
cordesgrandrue.slogan: A hilltop bastide that floats above the morning mists of the Cérou.
cordesgrandrue.line: Raimond VII, Count of Toulouse, founded the bastide in 1222; it was renamed Cordes-sur-Ciel in 1993 for its height above the valley clouds.
